sections.domain: Special signs, pavement markings and lane controls
sections.heading: C — Special signs, pavement markings and lane controls
sections.markdown:
## C — Special signs, pavement markings and lane controls

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
The shape of a route sign or marker tells you what kind of road you are on: Interstate, U.S., State or County highway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Bicycle and pedestrian crossing signs are black symbols on yellow and mark places, such as a shared use path meeting a road, where both bicyclists and walkers may cross. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
When passing or overtaking a bicyclist on any road, a driver must leave at least 3 feet of clearance, whether or not a white Pass 3 ft min sign is posted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
A white Bicycle May Use Full Lane sign reminds drivers that a bicyclist may ride in the middle of the lane when hazards or poor visibility would make riding on the right side unsafe. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle marks it as built to travel slower than 25 miles per hour. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Disabled parking signs, and markings painted in the space, reserve those spots for vehicles showing a disabled parking permit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
The crosshatched area next to a disabled space is for van access only, and no one may park there at any time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
You may park in a disabled space only when the person who holds the placard is getting into or out of the vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
Parking in a disabled space without a placard or plate can be charged as a misdemeanor, with a $350 to $5,000 fine on conviction, plus possible jail, loss of driving privileges or impoundment of the car. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
Using somebody else's placard or plate to park in a disabled space brings jail time, loss of driving privileges, towing and fines twice the normal amounts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
Pavement lines and symbols divide lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed, mark turn lanes and pedestrian walkways, and show where to stop for signals or signs. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
Yellow lines divide traffic going in opposite directions; a broken yellow line means passing is allowed. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
A solid yellow line, or a pair of solid yellow lines, means no passing, except that you may pass a bicyclist with at least three feet of room when the oncoming lane is clear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
With a solid and a broken yellow line side by side, you may not pass if the solid line is on your side, but may pass safely if the broken line is on your side, returning to your lane before the broken line becomes solid. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
Crossing a solid yellow line is allowed, when safe, for a left turn into a driveway, alley or private road, or to get around a bicyclist with three or more feet of room. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A01
White lines separate lanes moving the same way: a broken white line allows a safe lane change, and a solid white line means stay in your lane and also marks the road shoulder. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A01
Green paint marks a lane or area set aside for bicyclists and makes riders more visible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A01
Sharrows, or shared lane markings, warn that a lane may be too narrow for a car and a bicycle side by side, and bicyclists may ride in the center of such a lane or whenever they must avoid obstacles or be seen. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk, marked or unmarked, is where pedestrians have the right-of-way, and drivers must slow down or stop as needed for people crossing in it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A01
If a vehicle ahead is stopped at a crosswalk, you may not pass it; stop behind it, or behind the crosswalk in the next lane on a multi-lane road. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A01
Conflict zones are broken lines in a bike or bus lane warning drivers and bicyclists that their paths will cross there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A01
As a general rule, drive on the right half of the road and keep to a single lane without straddling two. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A02
Restricted lanes, such as transit or bicycle lanes, are reserved for a special use shown by signs or markings, often a white diamond painted in the lane or a roadside sign. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A02
Bike lanes are only for bicyclists and other authorized users, who have the right-of-way there; drivers may not drive, idle, park in or otherwise block a bike lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A02
A bike lane continues through an intersection even where no paint joins the two sides. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A02
Transit lanes are parts of the street marked by signs and markings for buses or light rail, sometimes with limited use by other vehicles allowed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A02
High Occupancy Vehicle lanes carry a painted white diamond, and signs state which vehicles may use them and how many occupants each needs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A02
A two-way left-turn lane, or center turn lane, is only for drivers turning left from either direction; you may wait in it until the turn is safe but may not use it to pass or travel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A02
If a street has a shared center turn lane, every left turn must be made from that lane and not from any other. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A02
On a road with no lane signs or markings, drive just right of the center, stay off the shoulder, and follow the same passing and turning rules as on marked roads. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A02
In a roundabout, traffic circles to the right around a center island, and drivers entering yield to traffic already circulating. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A02
Colorado law requires you to yield to a truck, bus, emergency vehicle or recreational vehicle entering, leaving or driving in a roundabout, and when two such large vehicles meet there, the one on the right yields to the one on the left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A02
Approaching a roundabout with no large trucks present, yield to traffic coming from the left, and do not stop fully unless traffic keeps you from merging. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A02
Each time you enter or exit a roundabout, give way to anyone walking or riding in a crosswalk and to vehicles already circling, and use turn signals to change lanes and to exit. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A02
Reversible lanes carry traffic one way at some times and the other way at other times, and are set apart by a barrier or double broken yellow lines, sometimes with signs or special lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A02
A diverging diamond interchange shifts traffic to the opposite side of the road across the interchange so vehicles can move onto freeway ramps without interruption. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0013]
